key_insight: Masked discrete diffusion can serve as a unified, non-autoregressive backbone for both multimodal understanding and generation, enabling a single model to predict and generate discrete multimodal tokens efficiently and flexibly.
problem_solved: Replaces the dominant autoregressive MLLM backbone to address inefficiencies, modality-specific pipelines, and the lack of a unified approach for both multimodal understanding and generation.
method: Encode multimodal data (e.g., text, image tokens) into discrete token streams and train a masked discrete diffusion model to reconstruct masked tokens.
Use the same diffusion-based model for conditional generation and understanding by applying different masking/conditioning schemes during sampling and inference.
Leverage mask scheduling and accelerated sampling techniques to balance reconstruction quality and inference efficiency for practical multimodal tasks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a single, scalable alternative to autoregressive architectures that unifies multimodal tasks, improves parallelism, and simplifies model design for both understanding and generation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multimodal inputs → tokenization → masked discrete diffusion backbone → conditional outputs (caption, image, etc.).
Side-by-side comparison chart: autoregressive vs masked discrete diffusion (parallelism, bidirectional context, unified tasks).
Pipeline example: conditional generation (text→image) and understanding (image→caption) workflows showing masking and sampling steps.
Mask scheduling timeline or animation illustrating progressive denoising/reconstruction of discrete tokens.
paper_title: Omni-Diffusion: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Masked Discrete Diffusion
paper_authors: Lijiang Li, Zuwei Long, Yunhang Shen, Heting Gao, Haoyu Cao
